subject: Perimeter delegation & port matrix for private deployment - Acme Health
messages:
From: Jim Porter <acme-devops@acmehealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Health Security <security@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-05-17T09:12:00Z
Subject: Onboarding: private runtime — initial perimeter asks

Marcus / Redwood team,

Thanks for the kickoff call this morning. To move the private deployment (VPC-attached) to our staging environment we need a short checklist from your side to get firewall and egress policy approved by our network team. Please provide the following:  

1) Definitive list of outbound IPs (and whether they’re static or ephemeral).  
2) Per-service port/hostname matrix (for control plane, telemetry, model pulls, metric sinks).  
3) Guidance on TLS interception (we do TLS inspection at the perimeter — any cert pinning we should be aware of?).  
4) Evidence of IP ownership/escrow (we prefer an attestation doc for our change board).  
5) A recommended temporary acceptance window (we typically allow a 48-72 hr open window for smoke tests).

I’ve attached our permitlist template (acme-permitlist-template.csv) for you to fill. Once we have the list and an IP attestation we can add entries and schedule a one-hour verification window with Ops. 

Also: our NAT mapping is somewhat constrained — we can provide a pool and a primary egress NAT if that helps with your routing. 

Thanks,
Jim Porter
Senior DevOps Engineer
Acme Health

--- attachment stub: acme-permitlist-template.csv (CSV template with columns: service, from_port, to_port, protocol, purpose, owner)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Jim Porter <acme-devops@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-17T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Onboarding: private runtime — initial perimeter asks

Jim — thanks for the clear list. I’m looping in our security and infra leads. High-level responses inline (we’ll follow with the artifacts you requested):

1) Outbound IPs: We will provide a single CIDR-sized allocation that maps to 6 static egress IPs for the control plane + telemetry and a small ephemeral pool for model fetches. Static IPs are published and we can include ASN and WHOIS evidence.

2) Port/hostname matrix: See the attached CSV (redwood-egress-ips-20260517.csv) — it lists the services, FQDNs and recommended destination ports. Quick summary: 443 TCP to redwood-control.redwood.ai (control plane), 443 TCP to s3-compatible endpoints for model pulls, 443 TCP to metrics.ingest.redwood.ai (optional). We do not require any inbound ports from your side for normal operation.

3) TLS inspection: Redwood’s runtime performs TLS on client->server for outbound calls. We do not perform certificate pinning that would break standard TLS interception, but we strongly recommend not breaking OCSP/CRL flows — best practice is to allow TLS inspection for our egress only when you can preserve full cert chains. If you must perform MITM-like interception, please notify us — some telemetry endpoints rely on certificate validation and we can provide fingerprint lists.

4) IP evidence: We’ll attach a signed IP attestation (short PoA) and a WHOIS snapshot. If your security team requires DocuSign, we can route the attestation for signature; see the DocuSign link we’ll generate in the next message.

5) Acceptance window: Propose 72 hours for the first smoke test (we’ll run health checks and synthetic prompt runs). If you prefer 48 hours, we can compress the verification tasks.

Runbook and tasks (high-level):
- Marcus: deliver IP list + MAP (today EOD).
- David: generate PoA and WHOIS evidence (today).
- Marissa: schedule verification window and Ops call with your team (tomorrow).

Attachments: redwood-egress-ips-20260517.csv, MAP-Proposal.md

Let us know your NAT mapping (pool + primary egress) so we can pin routes.

—
Marcus Lin
Enterprise Sales Lead
Redwood Inference
(attachment stub: redwood-egress-ips-20260517.csv)
(attachment stub: MAP-Proposal.md)
From: Jim Porter <acme-devops@acmehealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Health Security <security@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-05-17T11:48:00Z
Subject: Re: Onboarding: private runtime — initial perimeter asks

Marcus — thanks, that’s helpful. NAT mapping: we can allocate 3 primary NAT addresses for your static egress and a /28 for ephemeral outbound. Primary NATs: 198.51.100.10-12. Ephemeral pool: 198.51.100.32/28.

Security asks:
- We require a signed IP attestation with the CIDR and the purpose of traffic. Prefer DocuSign for auditability.
- Please include the expected TLS SNI list for telemetry/control endpoints so our inspection rules can maintain SNI/ALPN allowances.
- Can you confirm whether any of your endpoints perform mTLS? If so, which services and port pairs?

We’re happy to run the 72-hour window and will schedule the Ops verification for Friday at 09:00 PT if that works for your team.

Jim
--- (inline NAT mapping table)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Jim Porter <acme-devops@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-17T13:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Onboarding: private runtime — initial perimeter asks

Jim — perfect, thanks for the NAT ranges. Confirmations and next steps:  

- We’ll prepare a DocuSign attestation today and post the link to HubSpot. Expected contents: static IP list (6 addresses mapped to control/telemetry/model-fetch roles), CIDR for ephemeral pool, statement of purpose, and authorized signer.
- TLS SNI list: control.redwood.ai, metrics.ingest.redwood.ai, models-storage.redwood.ai. None of those endpoints require mTLS; we only use TLS client authentication for a small subset of partner integrations (we’ve noted none apply for this onboarding).
- Run the 72-hour window on Friday 09:00 PT — confirmed. We’ll provide the mutual-action-plan CSV before EOD and a short smoke-test checklist for your Ops run.

Attachments: mutual-action-plan-ACME.csv

Irene / David — can you review the attestation draft and sign once it’s ready?

Thanks — looking forward to getting this live.

—
Marcus Lin
Enterprise Sales Lead
Redwood Inference
(attachment stub: mutual-action-plan-ACME.csv)
